text: Schema drift and breaking changes — not every change to a contract is actually breaking.

Adding a new optional field is safe — a consumer reading specific fields is unaffected by one it never asked for. Renaming or changing the type of a field a consumer already relies on is breaking, no matter how small it looks.
A breaking change gets a new contract version, published alongside the old one, rather than edited in place. The old field stays deprecated but present during the transition.
Week one, both old and new fields are emitted. Consumers migrate over the following weeks at their own pace. Only then does the old field actually get removed.
Announced and staged, not silently substituted — exactly what prevents the surprise lesson 39's drift detection exists to catch. Next up: observability — logs, metrics, and traces.
